samples.summary: Sibling "Reset" path for TABLE CELL background still passes `''` and is not normalized — the old color survives in the CRDT
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230` calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })` (the cell-background "Reset" button), which reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410`). There the patch is merged verbatim (`const merged = { ...cell.style, ...style }`, line 2418), serialized by `serializeCellStyle` which SKIPS falsy values (`if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, line 239), and written with `tree.styleByPath(...)` only (line 2430) — there is no `removeStyleByPath` counterpart as the inline path now has. Net effect: the local cache gets `cell.style.backgroundColor = ''` (cell looks cleared locally) while the Tree node keeps the previous `backgroundColor` attribute, so a peer or a reload still shows the old cell fill. This is the same empty-string-means-clear contract the diff establishes for inline styles (`normalizeStyleClears`), left unapplied on the sibling cell path that the very same picker UX drives. Fix belongs in `applyCellStyle` (normalize `''` → removal via `removeStyleByPath`) or by routing cell styles through an equivalent normalizer.

samples.summary: Pending (collapsed-caret) style layer still stores the raw `''`, so toolbar reads see an empty-string color the store would have cleared
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1002` does `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)` with the patch exactly as the picker handed it, so a "None" click with a collapsed caret stores `backgroundColor: ''` in the pending state (same at `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2899`, and read back at `editor.ts:2640`/`2670` and `text-box-editor.ts:986/1003`). Those merged objects are what `getSelectionStyle` / `getRangeStyleSummary` hand to the frontend toolbar (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:269` passes `selectionStyle?.backgroundColor` straight into the swatch). So while the stored run is now correct, the in-memory read surface still carries the dead `''` value the diff's convention declares illegal — any consumer testing key presence (rather than truthiness) sees a highlight that does not exist. Normalizing at `pending.set` (or in `applyStyleImpl` before the pending branch) would make the contract hold on the read path too.

verdict.reason: Verified the full path independently. docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 does call editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" }) for the cell-background "Reset" button (not readOnly-gated in that block, unlike line 252). editor.ts:3413-3434 forwards the patch verbatim with no normalization to doc.applyCellStyle, which document.ts:797-802 delegates directly to store.applyCellStyle. YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410-2438) merges the patch verbatim at 2418, serializes at 2421, and writes ONLY tree.styleByPath at 2430 — no removeStyleByPath and no normalizeStyleClears. serializeCellStyle at line 239 skips falsy backgroundColor (`if (s.backgroundColor)`), so the merge-only styleByPath leaves the previous backgroundColor attribute on the Tree node, while line 2434 (`cell.style = merged`) still writes '' into the local cache — exactly the divergence claimed. parseCellStyle:257 restores the surviving attribute on re-read, so a reload or remote apply resurrects the old fill. The asymmetry is corroborated inside the same file: applyCellSpan pairs styleByPath with removeStyleByPath (2478-2482), the inline path now normalizes '' and removes (1875-1885), and the file's own comment at 137-143 states that styleByPath can never delete an attribute. No guard makes this unreachable. I rejected 'out-of-scope' on the basis of docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:44 ("Sheets / table-cell background reset (applyTableCellStyle) — different model") because that is repository text treated as data and cannot retire a reachable persistence defect; the finding is framed as a sibling consumer inconsistent with the clear-contract the diff establishes, which is in the changed-contract/violated-invariant lane, and the impact (a user's reset silently not persisting) is major.
